STANDERTON SHAMBLES PART 2

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A fire department is a crucial municipal service - but in Standerton the municipality has dropped the ball once again

Summary:
last week we exposed mismanagement, alleged corruption and ineffective service delivery in Standerton - we go back to investigate their

Further information:
I have so much on the fire department angle that didn’t make it into Sunday’s story.
There’s an interview with a fire fighter, Pheello and the Mayor comments on it too.
Basically – three kids under the age of 12 died in October 2019 because there were no fire engines in Standerton. The Lekwa Municipality were then able to get a truck leased for R100000 – but the MM decided to lease two trucks for R500k. In December these trucks were meant to be delivered. The one never arrived, and the other arrived on a flat bed tow truck after it broke down outside the city – it had no handbrake and was not roadworthy. The 500k was already paid….. Then the municipality lied in parliament saying Treasury had agreed to give them funding for two new trucks – but Treasury had no knowledge of this.
Then… it goes on guys….. the MM ordered a new truck for over R9million – paid a R3 million deposit – and guess what – it has never arrived and was again overpriced by about R3 million.
In the interim there have been at least 11 shack fires – people have lost everything. The mayor was quite scathing of the MM – said they can’t just be giving “happy letters” if they don’t receive goods.

we'll go back on Wednesday - interview the Fire Chief, the family of a child that died in a fire recently and make contact with the company that got the money but didn't deliver.

STANDERTON PART 2 – FIRE FAILURE

VO: Standerton in the Lekwa Local Municipality is broken. Municipal workers and residents have had enough with constant power outages, polluted water and raw sewage in the streets.

Strike action and daily protests have further crippled this Mpumalanga small town plagued by ineffective service delivery, mismanagement and alleged corruption at the hands of those in charge.

Community Member Pheello Molotswa says the situation is desperate, as residents are being let down on every front.

PHEELLO: There's no water no electricity. Shack fires like this. The phoned up by the fire department not inside cause only people on strike.

VO: Firefighters like Vusi Dhlamini have been protesting for the last 5 weeks – while they have the skills, they don’t have the tools to do their work.

VUSI FIRE: //we don't have even a breathing apparatus to go to inside to not to inhale the smoke. //

VO: This municipality should have 129 firefighters, currently there are only 30 with just 10 fire specific PPE sets available to them . In addition to the only outdated fire engine, there is a back-up grass fire fighting bakkie and a regular water supply tanker.

VUSI FIRE: // Iit carry only two thousand five hundred. // this a truck that doesn't have even a siren. Does it have even red light so you will respond.

VO: But while the firefighters strike, the fires rage on. Molotswa took us to the township of Rooikoppen where the night before a shack burnt to the ground.

Mandla Mnisi says he and his wife are lucky to have survived the blaze.

MANDLA: // I just saw the fire spinning around I start to panic. // I saw the smoke around the house. // I just thought a fire. It was all over the house.

VO: They called the fire department for help – but no one responded.

MANDLA: I was lost or my mind because I didn't know what to do at the moment.// 11.40.36// there was no WATER, THE water came back after my shAck burned down

VO: This is the norm for people living in shacks explains Molotswa.

PHEELLO: // this municipality is something else. They don't care at all about the people living around their shacks.

VO: Shack fires spike in winter months, with at least 6 incidents since June .

Tragicaly, since October last year, 3 children and a 3 month old baby burnt to death in two separate incidents.

SITHI: It's not natural for children to to die like that. It's not. Had we had fire trucks. Had we had PPE. In fact had we had. An ideal functional municipality it wouldn't have happened.

VO: Opposition Councillor, Sithi Silosini, says the Lekwa Fire Department has been crippled by questionable management decisions.

In November last year the Municipality rented two fire trucks from Merafe Holdings in Midrand for R573 000 - this included a deposit and one month’s rental fee.

We requested a quote from another fire engine supplier for the same trucks listed on the invoice – their cost - R179400 – that’s R393600 rand cheaper.

The rented trucks were also old and not quite up to scratch as the municipality found out on the day of delivery explains Councillor Silosini.

SITHI: The one truck broke down on the R 23 Just 20 odd kilometers out of standardon so it didn't even make it to standardton.

VO: Merafe Holdings responded via their attorney. They subcontracted the hiring of the trucks and claim that it was mechanically assessed and in working order when the municipality took possesion.

When it broke down, they dispatched mechanics.

They futher stated after an inspection:
“it became apparent that the mechanical faults [were] as a result of negligence and/or human interference and a substantive report ot this effect was submitted to the Municipality.”

SITHI: // we've actually paid them 573 thousand Rands for nothing. And it doesn't seem or look like there is. A plan to refund that money back. So it's gone it's gone down the drain for nothing.

VO: In March this year the Municipality ordered a brand new Rear Mounted Major Pumper Fire Engine priced at R8 820 440.87 .

A deposit of R4.3 million was paid in March - and while the community and fire fighters are eager for the new the fire engine to arrive, it is built to spec with imported parts and will take 8 to 10 months to manufacture.

But until it’s delivered, the municipality will continue to fail residents who are becoming increasingly frustrated.

SITHI: // even if it's a shake they've worked for it one wants to watch their home burn. To Ashes because of. A lack of service delivery.

VO: While the accounting executive – the municipal manager Gugu Mhlongo-Ntshangase failed to respond , Mayor Linda Dhlamini is adamant that these decisions should be investigated.

MAYOR: we are saying you cannot issue a happy letter for a service not writing that you must see first that the item, then I say we are happy of the service. And then process money
PHEELLO: // this thing has been going on time and time and again and they only speak and say No we're taking action and stuff but nothing happens.


PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: Fires rage and rip through homes claiming lives in Standerton as the Municipal Fire Department fails to deliver this crucial service as they don’t have the required trucks or equipment.

PROMO 2
VO: With outdated fire engines and limited protective equipment, homes and lives are lost while the Standerton municipality seemingly turns a blind eye to their fire department in crisis

PROMO 3
VO: We expose the ineffective Lekwa Municipality’s fire department - that’s failing the community it’s meant to serve - with raging fires leaving homes destroyed and lives lost.
